question: The Iron Age site named Tekwada is located in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Iron Age archaeological site of Tekwada is located in Maharashtra. It is associated with early iron-using (megalithic) cultures of the region. (तेकवाड़ा — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Iron Age in India (roughly from about 1200–1000 BCE) saw the spread of iron tools and is linked with the Painted Grey Ware (PGW) and megalithic cultures.

• Maharashtra has several important megalithic and early historic sites.

NOTE

• Other early iron sites in India include Malhar, Dadupur (UP) and Hallur (Karnataka), which show early evidence of iron working.

question: Rabindranath Tagore referred to ____________ as Nritya Samragini, which translates to 'the empress of dance'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitara Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rabindranath Tagore referred to Sitara Devi as "Nritya Samragini" (the empress of dance) after being impressed by her performance. She was a legendary Kathak dancer. (सितारा देवी — नृत्य साम्राज्ञी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sitara Devi (1920–2014) was born in Kolkata to a Kathak family; she received the Padma Shri and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms, originating in North India.

NOTE

• Mrinalini Sarabhai and Rukmini Devi Arundale were famous Bharatanatyam exponents; Rukmini Devi founded Kalakshetra in Chennai.

question: The term 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are associated with which crop in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paddy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aus", "Aman" and "Boro" are the three main cropping seasons/varieties of rice (paddy), especially in West Bengal, Assam and Bangladesh. (धान की तीन फसलें)

◦ Aus (autumn/pre-monsoon), Aman (winter/main kharif crop) and Boro (summer, irrigated).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rice is a kharif crop requiring high temperature (above 25°C) and high humidity/rainfall (above 100 cm).

• India is one of the largest producers of rice; West Bengal is the leading rice-producing state.

NOTE

• Cropping seasons in India: Kharif (sown June–July, e.g., rice, maize, cotton), Rabi (sown Oct–Dec, e.g., wheat, gram) and Zaid (summer, e.g., watermelon, cucumber).

question: How many chances does a high jumper get for overcoming a certain height?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three chances.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the athletics event of the high jump, a jumper gets three chances (attempts) to clear a particular height. Three consecutive failures (at any height) eliminate the athlete. (हाई जंप — तीन प्रयास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The high jump is a track-and-field event where athletes jump over a horizontal bar; the popular technique is the "Fosbury Flop".

• The same "three attempts" rule applies to events like the long jump, pole vault (per height) and shot put/discus/javelin (in the final rounds).

NOTE

• Athletics is governed internationally by World Athletics (formerly IAAF). The men's high jump world record (2.45 m) is held by Javier Sotomayor of Cuba.

question: Which of the following is the correct statement about the Rajya Sabha?
option_1: All the members are directly elected by the people.
option_2: It is known as the Council of the States.
option_3: It is known as the lower house of the parliament.
option_4: The term of the members is for 5 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is known as the Council of the States.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Indian Parliament and is known as the "Council of States". Its members are indirectly elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies. (राज्य सभा — राज्यों की परिषद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house (it is never fully dissolved); one-third of its members retire every two years, so each member's term is 6 years (not 5).

• The Lok Sabha is the lower house (House of the People), directly elected for a 5-year term.

• Maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated by the President).

NOTE

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Article 80 deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha.

question: Which Census decade recorded the highest population growth rate (in terms of percentage) in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1961-1971.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Census decade 1961–1971 recorded the highest decadal population growth rate (about 24.8%) in India's census history. (सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर — 1961-71)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The year 1921 is called the "Great Divide/Demographic Divide" — after it, India's population began growing rapidly and continuously.

• The 2001–2011 decade showed a growth rate of about 17.7%, lower than earlier decades, indicating a slowing of growth.

NOTE

• The first census in India was conducted in 1872 (under Lord Mayo) and the first complete/synchronous census in 1881 (under Lord Ripon). The census is conducted every 10 years.

question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is William Jones.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Asiatic Society of Bengal" was founded by Sir William Jones in 1784 at Calcutta (Kolkata) to promote the study of Indian history, languages, literature and culture. (एशियाटिक सोसाइटी ऑफ बंगाल — विलियम जोन्स, 1784)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sir William Jones was a British judge and Orientalist who noted the similarity between Sanskrit, Greek and Latin, laying the basis for the study of the Indo-European language family.

• The Society did pioneering work in deciphering ancient inscriptions and reviving interest in India's past.

NOTE

• Warren Hastings (Governor-General) was a patron of Orientalist studies and set up the Calcutta Madrasa (1781). James Prinsep, who deciphered the Brahmi script, was also associated with the Society.

question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights entails trafficking of human beings and forced labour?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rights against Exploitation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Right against Exploitation" (Articles 23 and 24) prohibits trafficking of human beings, begar (forced labour) and the employment of children below 14 years in hazardous work. (शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 23-24)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 23 — prohibits human trafficking and forced labour.

• Article 24 — prohibits child labour in factories, mines and hazardous employment.

• The six Fundamental Rights are: Right to Equality (14–18), Right to Freedom (19–22), Right against Exploitation (23–24), Right to Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural and Educational Rights (29–30) and Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

NOTE

• Fundamental Rights are given in Part III (Articles 12–35) of the Constitution and are largely inspired by the US Bill of Rights.

question: The weaker warm storms that grow stronger over time are finally converted into huge storms or hurricanes. Which of the following climate regions is the origin of such hurricanes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical climate region.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hurricanes (tropical cyclones) originate over the warm ocean waters of the tropical climate region, where the sea-surface temperature is high (above about 27°C), providing the heat and moisture needed for the storm to grow. (उष्णकटिबंधीय जलवायु क्षेत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• These storms are called hurricanes in the Atlantic/eastern Pacific, typhoons in the western Pacific, and cyclones in the Indian Ocean.

• The calm centre of a hurricane is called the "eye".

NOTE

• Tropical cyclones need warm seas, high humidity and the Coriolis force to form; they do not form right at the equator (where the Coriolis force is zero).

question: The author of the Hindi novel 'Kohre Mein Kaid Rang' is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Govind Mishra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindi novel "Kohre Mein Kaid Rang" was written by Govind Mishra, a distinguished Hindi novelist and short-story writer. (कोहरे में कैद रंग — गोविंद मिश्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Govind Mishra won the Sahitya Akademi Award (2008) for this novel and later received the Vyas Samman and Saraswati Samman.

• He is known for novels dealing with human relationships and the middle-class experience.

NOTE

• Kamleshwar (Kitne Pakistan), Uday Prakash (Peeli Chhatri Wali Ladki) and Chitra Mudgal (Aavan) are other noted Hindi writers.

question: In which of the following states is the Bissu Mela organised to thank Santoora Devi for the good harvest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Bissu Mela" is a traditional fair organised in Uttarakhand (in the Jaunsar-Bawar region) to thank the goddess Santoora Devi for a good harvest and to celebrate the spring/new agricultural season. (बिस्सू मेला — उत्तराखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The fair features folk songs, dances (like the Thoda dance) and community feasting.

• Uttarakhand is known as "Dev Bhoomi" (Land of the Gods) and has many pilgrimage and cultural fairs.

NOTE

• Famous fairs of Uttarakhand include the Kumbh Mela (Haridwar), Nanda Devi Raj Jat Yatra and Uttarayani Mela (Bageshwar).

question: In june 2022, Eknath Sambhaji Shinde became the Chief Minister of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Eknath Sambhaji Shinde became the Chief Minister of Maharashtra in June 2022, after a split in the Shiv Sena, with the support of the BJP (Devendra Fadnavis became Deputy CM). (एकनाथ शिंदे — महाराष्ट्र के मुख्यमंत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Maharashtra is India's second-most populous state; its capital is Mumbai (the financial capital of India) and winter capital is Nagpur.

• The Governor administers the oath of office to the Chief Minister (Article 164).

NOTE

• The Chief Minister is the real executive head of a state, while the Governor is the constitutional/nominal head.

question: Who among the following founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' in 1873?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jyotiba Phule.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Satyashodhak Samaj" (Society of Truth-Seekers) was founded by Jyotiba Phule (Jyotirao Phule) in 1873 at Pune (Maharashtra) to fight caste discrimination and untouchability and to uplift the lower castes and women. (सत्यशोधक समाज — ज्योतिबा फुले, 1873)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jyotiba Phule and his wife Savitribai Phule were pioneers of women's education and started one of the first schools for girls in India.

• Phule wrote "Gulamgiri" (Slavery), attacking the caste system, and coined the term "Dalit".

NOTE

• Phule was given the title "Mahatma". He worked for the education and rights of Shudras, Ati-Shudras (untouchables) and women.

question: Which type of loan is supported by MUDRA?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Non-farm loan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) supports non-farm (non-agricultural) micro and small enterprises by providing loans up to ₹10 lakh (now enhanced) for small businesses. (मुद्रा — गैर-कृषि ऋण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) was launched in 2015. Loans are given in three categories:

◦ Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000–₹5 lakh) and Tarun (₹5 lakh–₹10 lakh).

• These loans are collateral-free and aim to "fund the unfunded" small entrepreneurs.

NOTE

• MUDRA supports non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises such as shopkeepers, artisans, vendors and small manufacturers.

question: What is the percentage of 's' character in the carbon atom of acetylene?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In acetylene (C₂H₂, ethyne), each carbon atom is sp hybridised (it forms a triple bond). An sp hybrid orbital has one s and one p orbital, so the s-character is 1/2 = 50%. (एसीटिलीन — sp संकरण — 50% s-अक्षर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• s-character in common hybridisations:

◦ sp → 50% (e.g., acetylene/ethyne, triple bond),

◦ sp² → 33.33% (e.g., ethene, double bond),

◦ sp³ → 25% (e.g., methane/ethane, single bonds).

NOTE

• More s-character means the orbital is closer to the nucleus, so bonds are shorter and stronger, and the atom is more electronegative (this explains the acidity of terminal alkynes).

question: In Union Budget 2023, a sub-scheme of which of the following Yojanas has been proposed with the investment of ₹6,000 crore to enable activities of fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM Matsya Sampada Yojana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2023-24, a new sub-scheme of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) was announced with an investment of ₹6,000 crore to support fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises in the fisheries sector. (पीएम मत्स्य संपदा योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• PMMSY was launched in 2020 to bring about a "Blue Revolution" through sustainable development of the fisheries sector.

• The sub-scheme (PM-MKSSY) aims to improve value chains, formalise the sector and expand markets.

NOTE

• India is one of the largest fish producers in the world. The fisheries sector comes under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

question: India launched the 'National Social Assistance Programme' in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)" was launched on 15 August 1995. It provides social assistance (pensions and benefits) to the poor, elderly, widows and persons with disabilities. (राष्ट्रीय सामाजिक सहायता कार्यक्रम — 1995)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• NSAP is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Rural Development and gives effect to the Directive Principles (Article 41 — right to assistance in old age, sickness and disablement).

• Its components include the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme, Widow Pension Scheme, Disability Pension Scheme and the National Family Benefit Scheme.

NOTE

• NSAP targets Below Poverty Line (BPL) households, providing a basic level of financial support to the most vulnerable sections of society.

question: Which of the following Mughal emperors issued silver coins in the honour of his wife Mehrunnisa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jahangir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mughal emperor Jahangir issued silver coins in the honour of his wife Mehrunnisa (Nur Jahan), who wielded great influence in his court. (जहांगीर — नूरजहाँ के सम्मान में सिक्के)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nur Jahan ("Light of the World") was the powerful queen of Jahangir; coins were struck in her name and royal orders (farmans) were issued under her seal.

• Jahangir (r. 1605–1627) was the son of Akbar and was known for his interest in painting and justice (the "Chain of Justice").

NOTE

• The Mughal succession: Babur → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb. Shah Jahan (Jahangir's son) built the Taj Mahal for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

question: To which of the following groups do whales belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mammalia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Whales belong to the class Mammalia (mammals), not fish. They are warm-blooded, breathe air through lungs, give birth to live young and feed them with milk. (व्हेल — स्तनधारी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Whales, dolphins and porpoises are aquatic mammals belonging to the order Cetacea.

• The blue whale is the largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth.

NOTE

• Key mammalian features: hair/fur, mammary glands (milk), a diaphragm for breathing, four-chambered heart and (usually) live birth. Other mammals include bats (fly) and humans.

question: Buddhadev Dasgupta was a famous instrumentalist of which of the following instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Buddhadev Dasgupta was a renowned Indian classical musician famous for playing the "Sarod". He belonged to the Senia Shahjahanpur gharana. (बुद्धदेव दासगुप्ता — सरोद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music, known for its deep, resonant sound.

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Other famous Sarod maestros include Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Ustad Amjad Ali Khan. The Santoor is associated with Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and the Sitar with Pandit Ravi Shankar.

question: Who among the following received the Padma Shri 2021 for Panthi folk dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Radhe Shyam Barle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Radhe Shyam Barle received the Padma Shri in 2021 for his contribution to the "Panthi" folk dance of Chhattisgarh. (राधे श्याम बारले — पंथी नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Panthi dance is performed by the Satnami community of Chhattisgarh, usually on Maghi Purnima to honour Guru Ghasidas.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India (after Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan).

NOTE

• Bhuri Bai (a Bhil/Pithora artist of Madhya Pradesh) also received the Padma Shri for painting. Folk dances are often recognised through the Padma awards.

question:
Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterised by _________.
a) an abnormally heavy body weight
b) an intense fear of losing weight
c) a distorted perception of weight
d) trying to lose weight by exercising excessively
solution_text:
The correct answer is c and d.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Anorexia Nervosa is a serious eating disorder characterised by:

◦ (c) a distorted perception of one's weight/body image (seeing oneself as overweight even when underweight), and

◦ (d) attempts to lose weight through excessive exercising, extreme dieting and self-starvation.

• It typically involves an abnormally LOW body weight and an intense fear of GAINING weight — so statements (a) "abnormally heavy body weight" and (b) "fear of losing weight" are the opposite of the truth. (एनोरेक्सिया नर्वोसा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• People with anorexia severely restrict food intake, leading to malnutrition and health complications.

• A related eating disorder is Bulimia Nervosa, marked by cycles of binge-eating followed by purging (vomiting).

NOTE

• Eating disorders are psychological/mental-health conditions and require both medical and psychological treatment.

question: Which of the following is NOT a physiographic division of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Tibetan Plateau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Tibetan Plateau" is NOT a physiographic division of India — it lies mainly in China (Tibet), to the north of the Himalayas. (तिब्बती पठार — भारत का भाग नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The six major physiographic divisions of India are:

◦ The Himalayan Mountains, The Northern Plains, The Peninsular Plateau, The Indian Desert (Thar), The Coastal Plains and The Islands.

NOTE

• The Peninsular Plateau is the oldest landmass of India; the Northern Plains are formed by the alluvium of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers.

question: Ujjwala was the mascot of which national sports event held in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khelo India Para Games 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ujjwala" was the official mascot of the first Khelo India Para Games 2023, held in New Delhi. (उज्ज्वला — खेलो इंडिया पैरा गेम्स 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Khelo India scheme was launched by the Government of India (2018) to revive the sports culture at the grassroots level.

• It includes the Khelo India Youth Games, University Games, Winter Games and the Para Games.

NOTE

• Mascots are used to promote sporting events; they usually reflect the culture or spirit of the host place. The Khelo India programme comes under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

question: In Harappan civilisation, cities were planned with the streets generally oriented along the __________ directions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is cardinal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Harappan (Indus Valley) civilisation, cities were carefully planned on a grid pattern, with streets and lanes generally oriented along the cardinal directions — North, South, East and West. (मुख्य दिशाओं — कार्डिनल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Harappan town planning featured a grid layout, an advanced covered drainage system, and buildings of standardised baked bricks.

• Cities were usually divided into a raised "Citadel" (west) and a "Lower Town" (east).

NOTE

• The four cardinal directions are N, S, E, W; the ordinal (intercardinal) directions are NE, NW, SE, SW. Major Harappan sites: Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan and Rakhigarhi.
